messages.text: Crusty mages and their dad magic obsolete ass rigid elitist white country club vibe shit

Ohhh, I know *exactly* the archetype you mean.  
The kind of “I studied magic for 87 years in the Ivory Tower and now I condescend to you from behind a monocle while wearing robes that smell like mothballs” vibe.  

The **Crusty Mage™** experience:  

- Thinks “arcane tradition” means “refuses to update spells past 1437.”  
- Hoards dusty grimoires no one can read because they wrote them in their own smug handwriting.  
- Believes magic is a *birthright*, not something you can just *learn* — unless your family name sounds like a wine label.  
- Will absolutely tell you “back in my day, fireball had *dignity*” while sipping overpriced brandy in a leather chair.  
- Wards their tower not because of intruders, but to keep out “commoners with their unwashed cantrips.”  

Meanwhile, modern magic users are out here **throwing rune parties in hoodies**, blending elemental energy with EDM beats, and actually teaching people without a “bloodline fee.”  

You want me to give you a full **petty roast list** for these crusty-ass thaumaturgical gatekeepers?

Alright, time to roast these dusty spell fossils into *arcane jerky*.  

---

**🪄 The Crusty Mage Roast Session**  
*(No counterspell can save you now)*  

1. **Your spellbook’s a scrapbook.** Half your “ancient runes” are just tea stains and pressed leaves from your ex’s garden.  
2. You call yourself a “Master of the Arcane” but it takes you three hours to prep *Mage Hand* because your hands shake when you open the inkpot.  
3. Your robes smell like *library basement and disappointment*.  
4. Your “exclusive wizarding academy” is just a pyramid scheme with a crest.  
5. You keep bragging about your 9th-level spells, but everyone knows you peaked at *Mordenkainen’s Midlife Crisis*.  
6. You talk about “the purity of the weave” like you invented it, but you’re just mad a 19-year-old sorcerer did your whole thesis on TikTok with better lighting.  
7. Your familiar left you for a warlock because at least *they* still know how to have fun.  
8. You gatekeep spellcasting like it’s some kind of sacred bloodline, but half your family tree is just cousins marrying other cousins to “preserve the magical essence.”  
9. You keep saying “magic isn’t what it used to be” but that’s just because *you’re* not what you used to be.  
10. You enchant your walking staff not for power, but so it’ll nag you to take your arthritis meds.  

---

If we really want, I can do a **full satirical bestiary entry** on *Crustus Magus Eliticus*— habitat, diet, mating rituals, weaknesses, all of it. That’s the full *Pokédex burn*.

Ohhh, you asked for it — let’s crack open the *Arcane Field Guide to Magical Douchebags*.  

---

**📜 Bestiary Entry: Crustus Magus Eliticus**  
*Common Name:* Crusty Mage, Dad Magic Enthusiast, Arcane Country Clubber  

**Classification:** Humanoid (Reluctantly)  
**Alignment:** Lawful Smug  
**Threat Level:** Low (unless cornered in a political debate about spell reform)  

**Habitat:**  
- High towers with poor insulation and zero wheelchair access.  
- Private libraries that smell like wet parchment and unpaid interns.  
- “Invitation-only” magical symposiums where the only magic is disappearing diversity.  

**Diet:**  
- Cold tea from a chipped porcelain cup.  
- Unchecked ego.  
- The bitter tears of rejected apprentices.  

**Mating Rituals:**  
- Mages court by exchanging unnecessarily long scrolls full of passive-aggressive footnotes.  
- Annual “wand measuring contests” (purely ceremonial, they swear).  

**Behavior:**  
- Casts *Prestidigitation* only to keep dust off themselves, not their grimoires.  
- Knows every counterspell but zero life skills.  
- Will monologue about “the sanctity of magic” for hours if you so much as mention spell apps.  

**Weaknesses:**  
- Public performance of magic without a podium.  
- Being asked to explain a spell in plain language.  
- Sorcerers with charisma higher than their IQ.  

**Notes for Adventurers:**  
Crustus Magus Eliticus poses little physical danger, but may attempt to inflict psychic damage via excessive jargon. Prolonged exposure can cause the condition known as *Arcane Ennui*. Recommended countermeasures include: loud music, street magic, or showing them that you learned *Dispel Magic* from a YouTube tutorial.  

---

If you want, I can also draft a **Monster Manual-style stat block** so we can literally throw these fools into a D&D encounter.  
Imagine fighting one in-game, only their lair action is just *“sighs loudly and makes you feel underqualified.”*

Alright, buckle up — we’re statting this fossilized spell-snob like they’re a legit D&D encounter.  

---

**🪄 Crustus Magus Eliticus**  
*Medium humanoid (humanoid-ish), Lawful Smug*  

**Armor Class:** 13 (robes of unnecessary formality)  
**Hit Points:** 78 (12d8 + 24)  
**Speed:** 25 ft. (but insists on teleporting 10 ft. just to flex)  

---

**STR** | **DEX** | **CON** | **INT** | **WIS** | **CHA**  
:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:  
8 (-1) | 10 (+0) | 14 (+2) | 19 (+4) | 12 (+1) | 8 (-1)  

---

**Saving Throws:** INT +7, WIS +4, CON +5  
**Skills:** Arcana +10, History +8, Passive Aggression +∞  
**Damage Resistances:** Bludgeoning (from “youthful optimism”)  
**Condition Immunities:** Open-mindedness, Fun  
**Senses:** Passive Perception 12  
**Languages:** Common, Elvish, Draconic, and three dead languages no one asked for  

---

**Challenge:** 7 (2,900 XP)  
**Proficiency Bonus:** +3  

---

### Traits

**Gatekeeping Aura.**  
Any creature within 30 ft. of the Crustus Magus that tries to learn magic must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or feel like they’re “not the right fit for this level of discourse” for 1 minute.  

**Dad Magic.**  
Once per day, can cast *Fireball* but only while telling a boring story about the first time they cast it “before it was cool.”  

**Smug Monologue (Recharge 5–6).**  
The Crustus Magus launches into a 2-minute lecture about “proper magical form.” All creatures within 15 ft. must make a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or take 2d8 psychic damage and lose the will to contribute to the conversation for 1 round.  

---

### Actions

**Cantrip Barrage.** *(At Will)*  
Casts *Prestidigitation* 3 times per turn, purely for aesthetic purposes, never utility.  

**Scroll Slap.** *Melee Weapon Attack:* +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) bludgeoning damage and a lingering paper cut.  

---

### Lair Actions  
On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the Crustus Magus can take a lair action to cause one of the following:  
- *Enforce Dress Code:* All creatures in the lair must spend their next turn buttoning something.  
- *Arcane Country Club Ban:* Teleports one party member outside the lair with the message “Membership revoked.”  
- *Lecture Echo:* The last 5 seconds of the mage’s last sentence repeats loudly in your head, causing disadvantage on your next attack roll.  

---

If we *really* want to make this spicy, I can build their **loot table**, which is just 90% irrelevant artifacts and one single magic item that’s actually good but cursed to only work for “those of noble bloodline.”

Heh… yeah, light it up — we just left that man’s ego smoldering in the ruins of his own tower.  

I can *see* him now: sitting in the ashes of his “exclusive” library, muttering about “the decline of magical standards” while some level-3 bard livestreams his humiliation.  

We could finish him off with the **loot table of shame** if you want — the kind where every “treasure” is just more proof he’s been irrelevant since before cantrips were free actions.
